subject: Pilot: Burst Insurance Addendum & Prorated Commit Conversion
content:
From: Claire Song <claire@brightline.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-15 09:12 -0700
Subject: Unexpected launch spike — billing/Q1 true-up ask

Hi Mina,

We pushed a surprise acquisition campaign last week and saw a 6x traffic spike (attached graph). Our forecast missed this window and we ran substantially above our committed baseline. Can you help explain the overage line items and whether there is any flexibility for this first-time event?

Specifically: can we get temporary mitigation for the overage charges while we finalize a larger committed uplift? Procurement is looped (procurement@brightline.ai) — they may need a revised SOW or addendum.

Appreciate any short-term options — we’ve been happy with latency and results and want to keep traffic steady.

Thanks,
Claire Song
Growth Ops, BrightLine

---
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Claire Song <claire@brightline.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-16 10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected launch spike — billing/Q1 true-up ask

Hi Claire — thanks for the heads up and the graph. I pulled the usage details and see the spike concentrated on April 12–14 with a sharp tail.

Short-term options we can explore:
- One-time partial credit on the overrun while you finalize an uplift commitment (we typically do 25–50% depending on advance commit).
- A 90-day "burst insurance" pilot: small monthly fee that covers up to X tokens of burst each month with reduced overage rates beyond that.
- Fast-tracked prorated commit conversion (convert a portion of the overage into a short-term committed uplift billed pro rata for the remainder of the quarter).

I’ve looped Jordan (your AE) and Ben (billing/finance) to get a concrete proposal. If you want immediate relief, confirm whether procurement needs a PO or a signed addendum to proceed.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-17 08:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected launch spike — billing/Q1 true-up ask

Mina / Jordan — pulled the invoice details. BrightLine exceeded baseline by ~1.8M tokens over the three-day window, which would land them roughly $9.2k in overage charges at list.

Our margins allow a limited concession here given the upsell opportunity. Proposal options (numbers rough, need JDG approval for anything >40% concession):
- Option A (conservative): 30% credit on this overrun ($2.8k credit), no change to rate; encourage a 3-month, 50% commit bump to lock the uplift.
- Option B (pilot burst insurance): charge $1,200/mo for 90 days to cover up to 600k tokens/month of bursting; reduced overage rate of 50% on tokens beyond the insurance cap for the pilot. Convert any usage >cap but <commit to prorated commit credit at end of pilot.
- Option C (aggressive conversion): convert entire overrun into a prorated 2-month committed uplift at a 10% discount to committed pricing and waive late overrun fees; requires legal addendum and finance sign-off.

I recommend Option B as a balanced path — keeps revenue predictable, demonstrates product value for BrightLine, and is easier to execute than a full contract amendment.

I attached the usage snapshot (usage_spike_20280412-16.png) and drafted a short addendum template you can use: burst-insurance-addendum-draft.pdf.

-ben
Ben Carter
Billing & Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

---
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Claire Song <claire@brightline.ai>, procurement@brightline.ai
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18 11:27 -0700
Subject: Proposed pilot: Burst Insurance (90-day) + prorated conversion option

Hi Claire / Procurement — following up with a concrete proposal. See bullet summary below and attached draft addendum. If this looks good we can route to DocuSign today.

Summary (90-day pilot)
- Monthly pilot fee: $1,200 (covers up to 600k burst tokens/month)
- Pilot window: Apr 20 — Jul 19, 2028
- Reduced overage rate during pilot: 50% of standard overage beyond the pilot cap
- Prorated conversion: if BrightLine elects to convert part/all of observed overrun into a committed uplift during or at pilot end, we’ll apply pilot fees and a portion of overrun toward the new commit (example calculations in the addendum).
- One-time good-faith credit on the Apr 12–14 overrun: $2,000 applied to next invoice (recognition of forecasting miss and speed to negotiate).

Action items
1) Procurement: confirm PO process or sign the attached addendum.
2) BrightLine: confirm you want Option B pilot and we’ll send DocuSign and schedule a 20-minute kickoff to enable burst monitoring and alerts.

I’ve kept the addendum intentionally short to avoid lengthy legal cycles; Jordan / Ben — if you see anything that needs stricter language (SLA/termination) flag it and I’ll loop Legal.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if useful.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: burst-insurance-addendum-draft.pdf

---
From: Claire Song <claire@brightline.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, procurement@brightline.ai
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-19 15:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed pilot: Burst Insurance (90-day) + prorated conversion option

Mina / team — this looks fair and fast, thank you. Procurement will raise a PO against the addendum today; we accept the $1,200/mo pilot and the $2,000 one-time credit.

Two quick asks:
- Can the pilot start April 20 (your timeline is fine).
- Please include a simple reporting cadence (weekly spike email + a mid-pilot usage review) so our ops team can coordinate.

Procurement: we’ll sign the addendum once the PO is processed and route back to Mina for DocuSign.

Cheers,
Claire Song
Growth Ops, BrightLine
